items.title: Microsoft tools to power Manulife's global transformation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Manulife has renewed and expanded its longstanding partnership with Microsoft under a five-year agreement aimed at accelerating its transformation into an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered organisation. As part of the expanded collaboration, Manulife has adopted Microsoft 365 E7 Frontier Suite capabilities to drive innovation through secure cloud and AI solutions across its global operations. Microsoft also serves as a foundational partner in Manulife's global enterprise AI platform, which is currently in pilot.

items.title: Abundance Treasures launches asset-backed P2P financing platform
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Abundance Treasures Group Sdn Bhd has launched Abundance Dynamic Securities (ADS), a peer-to-peer (P2P) financing platform specialising in asset-backed guaranteed financing. ADS connects mid-tier companies seeking larger funding with investors through a secure and transparent platform. The company also signed six memorandums of understanding (MoUs) during the soft launch with Koperasi Tenaga Nasional Bhd, Scrut Auto Sdn Bhd, Finzwerk Management, Stocktalk Holding Sdn Bhd, Pam Biz Financial Sdn Bhd and Hakem Arabi & Associates.

items.title: Panasonic to shut Shah Alam plant by March next year, 400 jobs affected
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Panasonic AVC Networks Kuala Lumpur Malaysia Sdn Bhd will cease operations at its Shah Alam facility by March 2027 as part of a global restructuring aimed at strengthening the competitiveness of its audio-visual consumer business. Production of Technics-branded Hi-Fi audio products will also end at the Shah Alam facility by February 2027 and be transferred to another Panasonic Group company. The Shah Alam facility currently manufactures Panasonic televisions, Blu-ray Disc players and components for Technics-branded audio products.

items.title: KL police transfer 113 refugees to new locations in three states
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — All 113 refugees temporarily housed at the Kuala Lumpur Contingent Police Headquarters (IPK) were transferred in stages yesterday following a document re-identification process, Kuala Lumpur Police Chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said. He said the refugees were bound for destinations in Kuala Lumpur, Selangor, and Penang, as determined by non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) based on the locations of their relatives and acquaintances. Fadil said 66 refugees were transferred to destinations in Kuala Lumpur, while 29 were transferred to Selangor and 18 to Penang.

items.title: Malaysia tightens hiking rules to cut costly mountain rescue operations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — The Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) is tightening controls on hiking activities nationwide, including restricting “day hikes” or “compressed hikes” in high-risk mountainous areas, to reduce accidents and the need for costly search and rescue (SAR) operations. Its Deputy Minister, Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh, said some hikers continue to underestimate the importance of proper preparation, while others are driven by social media trends or venture onto unauthorised trails, increasing the risk of emergencies and hikers getting lost in the forest. Syed Ibrahim said the Forestry Department of Peninsular Malaysia (JPSM) has also made the services of Forestry Mountain Guides (MGP) mandatory at 189 high-risk hiking locations nationwide.

items.title: Rice commercial stocks at 1.25 million tonnes as Mardi ramps up crop research
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's overall rice supply remains at a healthy level, with total trading stocks standing at 1.249 million metric tonnes as of July 14, including a 200,000 metric tonne stockpile capable of meeting national demand for 6.2 months. He said this includes ensuring that commercial and buffer rice stocks are maintained at optimal levels for immediate use in the event of disruptions to the country's rice supply chain. Malaysia currently imports rice from key source countries such as Thailand, Vietnam and India.

items.title: Vape excise duty reaches RM354.51mil as govt reviews controls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of RM354.51 million in excise duty has been collected from electronic cigarette or vape products between 2023 and June 11 this year. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said revenue collected from excise duties on vape products was not a justification for allowing the sale of such products. "For the period during which excise duty was imposed on electronic cigarette or vape products, the recorded tax collections amounted to RM80.32 million in 2023, increasing to RM111.14 million in 2024 and RM118.93 million in 2025.

items.title: Alliance Bank expects Malaysia GDP growth near 5pct
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Alliance Bank Bhd expects Malaysia's economy to grow towards the upper end of the government's four to five per cent forecast this year, backed by strong tourism, sustained foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows and proactive policy measures. Group chief executive officer Kellee Kam said the country entered the year from a position of strength, with robust domestic demand and continued business activity helping cushion external uncertainties. Kam said record tourism activity and strong FDI inflows have supported consumption and investment, while measures introduced by Bank Negara Malaysia and the government have strengthened the economy's resilience.

items.title: No bullying link to student's attempted jump, police confirm
items.summary: Terengganu police chief Datuk Mohd Khairi Khairudin said preliminary investigations found that the 14-year-old girl had been diagnosed with schizophrenia in May, a condition known to her parents and the school administration. Also present was Terengganu Education Department Student Development Sector deputy director Mohd Zulkafli Jusoh. He said police school liaison officers would also continue monitoring the case as a preventive measure.

items.title: Sentence no effect on Shafie as Senallang rep, says speaker
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The five-week jail sentence on former Sabah chief minister Datuk Seri Mohd Shafie Apdal does not affect his position as Senallang assemblyman. Sabah Legislative Assembly Speaker Datuk Seri Kadzim A. Yahya said the sentence imposed on the Parti Warisan president does not have any effect on his status as an assemblyman for the time being. "If it is a jail sentence, there is no effect.

items.title: Malaysia needs at least RM300m a year to secure permanent F1 return, says SIC CEO
items.summary: SEPANG, July 29 — Malaysia would need to spend at least RM300 million annually if it hopes to secure a permanent place on the Formula 1 (F1) world championship calendar, according to Sepang International Circuit (SIC) Chief Executive Officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif. He said the estimate covers Formula 1 hosting rights fees, currently estimated at between US$70 million and US$80 million (RM289 million to RM340 million), as well as local preparation costs required to meet the specifications for staging the prestigious race. He said there are two main requirements if Malaysia is to regain a permanent slot on the Formula 1 calendar: the ability to pay the hosting rights fees and the availability of a slot on the championship calendar.

items.title: Shafie's remarks 'cannot be shielded under the guise of free speech'
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The Sessions Court today ruled that Datuk Seri Mohd Shafie Apdal's remarks on the inquest into the death of Zara Qairina Mahathir were not protected by the right to free speech and amounted to serious contempt of court. Judge Amir Shah Amir Hassan said the court had evaluated the full recording and its context before concluding that Shafie's extrajudicial remarks "cannot be shielded under the guise of free speech". Earlier, Shafie was found guilty of contempt of court.

items.title: Malaysia told to reinvent Islamic finance to stay ahead
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's next challenge in Islamic finance is no longer building scale, but strengthening innovation as the industry seeks to expand beyond traditional banking and capital market offerings, the central bank said. Deputy governor Adnan Zaylani Mohamed Zahid said the country's comprehensive Islamic finance ecosystem has made it a global leader, but sustaining that position will require continued innovation and collaboration. Adnan said Islamic banking assets account for close to half of Malaysia's banking sector, while the Islamic capital market represents more than 60 per cent of the overall capital market.

items.title: Many young Malaysians can't tell zakat from charity, says Yayasan Hasanah
items.summary: Managing director and trustee Siti Kamariah Ahmad Subki said strengthening basic religious and financial knowledge is essential to help younger generations better understand Islamic finance and make informed financial decisions. Siti Kamariah said the gap stemmed from a gradual erosion of foundational religious knowledge that underpins Islamic finance. She said improving financial literacy alone would not be enough unless Islamic financial institutions also simplified their products, policies and communication.

items.title: Penang awaits Kedah's lease claim filing, says Chow
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang is waiting for Kedah to formally file its claim over the state's lease payments before responding, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said. Chow said the state government has maintained the same position despite Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor's latest remarks that all legal and historical documents for the claim are ready. Earlier this month, Chow said Penang was never consulted on the Sultan of Kedah's call for the federal government to review the state's lease payment.

items.title: Chow Kon Yeow: Penang to respond only after Kedah submits formal lease payment claim
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, July 29 — Penang will continue to wait for Kedah to formally submit its claim over the state’s lease payments before responding, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said today. He said this was not the first time Kedah Mentri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor had spoken about pursuing a revision of Penang’s lease payment rates. Asked whether the issue could strain relations between Penang and Kedah if the claim proceeds, Chow said it was premature to comment as Penang had yet to receive any formal demand.

items.title: Dr Mahathir's RM150mil defamation suit awaits medical update
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The High Court will be updated on Friday on Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad's condition and fitness to resume his RM150 million defamation suit against Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Dr Mahathir's lawyer, Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali, said a case management would be held online before judicial commissioner Datuk Donald Joseph Franklin. "It will not be easy due to Dr Mahathir's age and medical parameters," he said.

items.title: Top 10pct of formal workers earn at least RM11,500 a month
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's top 10 per cent of formal sector employees earned at least RM11,500 a month in March 2026, more than six times the wages of the country's lowest-paid workers. According to the Statistics Department, employees in the bottom 10 per cent received a monthly wage of RM1,700 or less, while those in the 90th percentile earned at least RM11,500 per month. Male formal employees, who accounted for 55.0 per cent or 3.88 million of the total workforce, received a median monthly wage of RM3,064, compared with RM3,000 for female formal employees, who represented 45.0 per cent or 3.17 million workers.

items.title: N9 polls: Kuala Pilah's heritage shophouses await revival
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: As polling day draws near, towns and villages across Negri Sembilan are filled with political flags, grand speeches and campaign machinery. Yet in Kuala Pilah, the pace is noticeably slower. With proper conservation and restoration, locals believe the royal town could one day rival the heritage streetscapes of George Town and Melaka.

items.title: Eppendorf inks lease for first Southeast Asia plant in Penang
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: German life science company Eppendorf SE today signed a lease agreement to establish its first Southeast Asia manufacturing facility at Bandar Cassia Technology Park. Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the investment reflected the confidence global industry leaders continued to place in Penang's industrial ecosystem while strengthening the state's capabilities in the scientific and measuring equipment sector. He said the investment would reinforce Penang's position in advanced manufacturing, healthcare and life sciences, while supporting the state's long-term ambition to build a competitive healthcare ecosystem.

items.title: Prasarana says 1.31 million daily riders helped avoid 225,000 tonnes of carbon emissions in 2025
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, July 29 — Prasarana Malaysia Berhad today announced that it avoided an estimated 225,000 tonnes of carbon emissions in 2025, based on public transport usage averaging 1.31 million passenger trips a day. Amir said the report, themed The City on the Move, is the first sustainability report published in Prasarana’s 28-year history. “Today, sustainability goes beyond environmental sustainability.

items.title: Younger customers don't care about Syariah contracts, says Bank Islam CEO
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Islamic banks risk losing relevance among younger customers if they fail to deliver seamless digital banking experiences, as consumers increasingly prioritise convenience over the technicalities of Syariah contracts. Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd group chief executive officer Raja Teh Maimunah Raja Abdul Aziz said banks should focus on delivering customer-centric digital services rather than emphasising the complexity of products behind the scenes. Customer centricity is everything," she said.

items.title: Police investigate Jempol MP after report over allegedly seditious campaign speech
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 29 —Police have opened an investigation paper against Jempol Member of Parliament Datuk Shamsulkahar Mohd Deli over a campaign speech in Seremban Jaya which was alleged to contain seditious elements. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the investigation was launched following a report lodged by a 55-year-old man who was dissatisfied with a social media video post showing the politician’s campaign speech. For the latest updates on the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election, visit https://prn.bernama.com/n9.

items.title: Senate confirms Jay Clayton as Trump intelligence chief
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US Senate confirmed Jay Clayton as Donald Trump's top intelligence official Tuesday, putting a permanent chief in charge of the country's spy agencies as the president revives unsupported election fraud claims ahead of the midterms. Senators voted 51-47 to confirm Clayton's appointment, with all Democrats in the upper chamber voting against it. Clayton takes over from acting director of national intelligence Bill Pulte, a Trump loyalist with no relevant experience whose brief tenure alarmed lawmakers in both parties.

items.title: Bridge funding gap for social finance graduates: Bank Negara deputy governor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Entrepreneurs emerging from social finance programmes often face a funding gap as they transition from community-based support to sustainable commercial ventures. This highlights the need for new risk-sharing models in the country's Islamic finance ecosystem, said Bank Negara Malaysia deputy governor Adnan Zaylani Mohamed Zahid. Islamic finance should go beyond providing financial services by creating wider socioeconomic impact, Adnan said.

items.title: Malaysian workers' pay hits record RM686.9bil in 2025
items.summary: As a result, labour's share of GDP increased to 33.9 per cent from 33.6 per cent a year earlier. Malaysia's nominal GDP grew 4.8 per cent to RM2.03 trillion in 2025, supported by growth across all economic sectors. However, its share of GDP slipped to 62 per cent from 63.6 per cent in 2024, while growth slowed to 2.1 per cent from 4.9 per cent due to weaker performance in the services, agriculture and construction sectors.

items.title: MACC to stay professional despite negative perceptions, says Abd Halim
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will continue to uphold professionalism, transparency and integrity despite negative perceptions surrounding its investigations, Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said. Such perceptions should not intimidate the agency as long as every investigation was conducted in accordance with the law, procedures and due process, he said. Perceptions will always exist, but confidence in the integrity of the process and the professionalism of our officers must be upheld," he said during the MACC podcast Kolar Hitam: Bukan Sekadar Operasi today.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia's key index close slightly higher at midday
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia's key index closed slightly higher at midday, with buying interspersed with selling in selected heavyweights amid a mostly weaker regional trend. At 12.30pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 0.82 of-a-point to 1,713.30 from yesterday's close of 1,712.48. Turnover totalled 1.63 billion shares worth RM1.01 billion.

items.title: Spending controls yield nearly RM5b savings without affecting key services, says Liew Chin Tong
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — The government has recorded nearly RM5 billion in savings as of July 14, 2026, from the implementation of expenditure control measures following the RM10 billion adjustment to the operating expenditure allocation for this year, said Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong. Liew said the Ministry of Finance (MOF) on April 29, 2026, issued directives to adjust allocations across all ministries and government agencies before holding engagement sessions to explain the expenditure control criteria needed to be implemented in response to the global supply chain crisis. He noted that the expenditure control measures implemented by the government in the first half of 2026 successfully improved the efficiency of public financial management without compromising the delivery of critical services to the people or the country’s economic stability.

items.title: Woman killed in three-car crash near school in Tasek Gelugor
items.summary: The victim, identified as Zuraini Jaafar, was trapped in her Perodua Kancil following the collision involving a Perodua Axia and a Proton Saga at 8.26am. Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations John Sagun Francis said firefighters from the Tasek Gelugor station were dispatched to the scene and arrived at 8.41am. "Our personnel used special rescue equipment to free the remaining trapped victim, who was pinned in the driver's seat.

items.title: South Korean stocks collapse amid Asian tech rout
items.summary: SK Hynix was crushed, shedding almost 20 per cent, having dived more than 14 per cent on Tuesday. Samsung plunged more than 12 per cent. Tokyo was also hit, diving around three per cent as chip firm Kioxia plunged 13 per cent, while Tokyo Electron was down 12 per cent.

items.title: Three surveyors found safe after getting lost during forest survey in Dungun
items.summary: DUNGUN, July 29 — Three male surveyors who were reported to have lost their way while carrying out land surveying work in a forest area in Kampung Tok Kah here were found safe in a search and rescue (SAR) operation last night. Dungun district police chief Supt Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said the victims, Wan Muhamad Haziem Wan Abdullah, 32, Wan Hafizuddin Aiman Wan Zamili, 23, and Muhammad Adam Ruzilan, 22, were found at 11.30 pm. He said the three victims entered the forest area at 10 am yesterday with three other colleagues to carry out land surveying work, before they split into two groups at the location.

items.title: Toyota to halt operations at 3 southern Japan plants through Friday after earthquake
items.summary: TOKYO: Toyota will suspend operations at three plants in the southern region of Kyushu from the second production shift on Wednesday through Friday due to the impact of an earthquake in the area, the automaker said in a statement. "The situation, including aftershocks and recovery efforts, is changing daily. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Negeri Sembilan polls: Police receive 62 reports, open 19 investigation papers over offences
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 29 — Three investigation papers were opened yesterday, bringing to 19 the total number of investigation papers opened by police for election offences since campaigning for the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election began on July 18. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said police received 62 reports on election-related offences during the same period. He said the investigation papers opened yesterday included one involving an offence under Section 11 of the Election Offences Act 1954 for committing bribery.

items.title: Forest City backs permanent police presence after scam syndicates busted
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Forest City has expressed support for a permanent police presence within the township, days after a joint enforcement operation dismantled two online scam syndicates operating from its apartments and bungalows. In a statement, Forest City commended the police, Home Ministry, Immigration Department and other enforcement agencies for the operation, saying it reflected the government's comitment to upholding the rule of law and combating organised crime. Forest City said it welcomed the establishment of a permanent police presence within the township, saying a dedicated police station or service centre would strengthen crime prevention, improve emergency response and provide more accessible policing for residents, businesses and visitors.

items.title: Perceptions won't deter MACC investigations, says chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will continue to uphold professionalism, transparency and integrity despite negative perceptions surrounding its investigations. MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said such perceptions should not intimidate the agency as long as every investigation is conducted in accordance with the law, procedures and proper processes. Perceptions will always exist, but confidence in the integrity of the process and the professionalism of officers must be upheld," he said during the MACC podcast Kolar Hitam: Bukan Sekadar Operasi today.

items.title: Johor father charged with murder after 18-month-old’s death reclassified three years later
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, July 29 — A 40-year-old customer service officer was charged in the Magistrate's Court today with the murder of his 18-month-old son and with possessing pornographic material. The accused, G. Thevendhiran, acknowledged the charges read before Magistrate Nurzihan Abdul Rehman. The case took a dramatic turn yesterday when police upgraded the investigation into the infant's death to a murder case.

items.title: UBS logs forecast-beating quarterly profit, flags US$3 billion in new buybacks by end-June
items.summary: Net profit attributable to shareholders for Switzerland's biggest bank came in at US$2.8 billion, compared with a forecast of US$2.39 billion in a company-provided poll of analysts. The share buyback plans follow US$3 billion worth of buybacks completed in July. Analysts had forecast UBS would conduct some US$4.45 billion worth of buybacks during 2026.

items.title: Bukit Aman announces 25 senior cop transfers, promotions
items.summary: Bukit Aman Special Branch E6 principal assistant director Deputy Commissioner Datuk Mohd Taufik Toh Abdullah will also be promoted to Commissioner of Police as Special Branch 1 deputy director. Bukit Aman CID (D7) Organised Crime/Detention/Supervision principal assistant director Senior Assistant Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Farouk Eshak will serve as Bukit Aman CID Forensic/Strategic Planning deputy director with the acting rank of Deputy Commissioner. Two other Senior Assistant Commissioners elevated to Acting Deputy Commissioner are Sabah Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department chief Datuk Mohd Azhar Hamin, who becomes Sabah deputy police commissioner, and Bukit Aman Special Branch E4A assistant director Roslan Alias, who takes over as Bukit Aman Special Branch E6 principal assistant director.

items.title: Rohingya refugees relocated to KL, Selangor, Penang after police documentation process [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The 113 Rohingya refugees brought to the Kuala Lumpur police headquarters after being relocated from outside the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) office have been moved to new accommodation in Kuala Lumpur, Selangor and Penang. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the documentation and identity verification exercise was conducted at Dataran Wira within the Kuala Lumpur police headquarters from 12.01am to 4.30pm on Tuesday. He said the group travelled to three destinations — Kuala Lumpur, Selangor and Penang — with most using e-hailing services to reach their destinations.

items.title: Govt to refine cost-of-living indicators for more targeted policies, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — The government will continue to advance and refine the development of official statistics to support more accurate and effective policymaking, including through the production of more granular indicators, said Deputy Economy Minister Datuk Mohd Shahar Abdullah. Mohd Shahar said the government developed the Cost of Living Indicator in 2024, which measures the cost of living in greater detail based on data from the Household Income, Expenditure and Basic Amenities Survey and the Consumer Price Index, to ensure a more accurate depiction of household spending patterns. To date, cost-of-living indicators, including the Basic Expenditure of Decent Living (PAKW) Index, Cost of Living and Average PAKW Index, are available down to the administrative district level.

items.title: Anwar steps up Negeri Sembilan campaign push with packed final stretch schedule
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has a packed schedule in Negeri Sembilan today as he steps up Pakatan Harapan’s (PH) campaign ahead of polling day for the state election this Saturday. Anwar, who is also Pakatan Harapan chairman, is also scheduled to lead two Grand Finale Kekal Harapan Negeri Sembilan campaign events, which will also be attended by the coalition’s top leadership. Also expected to be present are Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu, PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, PH communications director and PKR information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, as well as PH candidates contesting the state election.

items.title: Warisan president Shafie Apdal sentenced to five weeks’ jail for contempt over Zara Qairina claims, gets stay pending appeal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — The Kota Kinabalu Sessions Court has sentenced Warisan president and Semporna MP Datuk Seri Shafie Apdal to five weeks in prison for contempt of court over remarks regarding the inquest into the death of 13-year-old Zara Qairina Mahathir. However, judge Amir Shah Amir Hassan stayed the execution of the sentence, allowing Shafie to remain free pending his appeal against the conviction in the High Court, FMT reported. The contempt charges stem from an event in Kinabatangan in September last year, where Shafie reportedly characterised Zara’s death as “murder” and questioned the authorities’ handling of the case.

items.title: Man, two boys rescued after going missing during forest outing near Dungun waterfall
items.summary: Dungun Fire and Rescue Station chief Yahaya Hanafi said the victims were Izham Haziq Mohd Ridhuan, 23, and Muhammad Harraz Naufal Zamri and Ahmad Al Baihaqi Ahmad Nazri, both aged 10. “Preliminary investigations found that the victims had gone to the waterfall with several friends for a swim. Yahaya said the SAR operation involved seven firefighters from the Dungun and Paka fire and rescue stations, three police personnel and 30 members of the public.

items.title: Sanusi: Kedah ready to challenge Penang lease rates, awaiting ‘right moment’ for legal move
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — The Kedah state government has finalised the historical research and legal groundwork required to pursue a revision of Penang’s lease payment rates, Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor claimed when saying the state is now waiting for the optimal moment to strike. The move follows a royal decree by the Sultan of Kedah, Sultan Sallehuddin Sultan Badlishah, on July 5. Chow further said that Penang has received no formal legal correspondence from Kedah, despite Muhammad Sanusi’s assertions that a legal team had been assembled.

items.title: KTMB boosts Komuter and ETS services for Negeri Sembilan election, pauses KVDT2 works
items.summary: To handle the influx, KTMB is adding 36 extra Komuter trips. Passengers heading toward Seremban or Pulau Sebang via the Tanjung Malim route can transfer at KL Sentral. KTMB has introduced 30 extra ETS trips, adding 9,480 seats across three key routes: 12 trips between KL Sentral and JB Sentral, 12 between JB Sentral and Seremban, and six between KL Sentral and Padang Besar.

items.title: Berjaya Hills loses legal battle over retroactive quit rent charges in Pahang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — The Court of Appeal has rejected five appeals by Berjaya Hills Resort Bhd and several landowners, upholding the Pahang state government’s right to revise quit rent rates without needing the National Land Council to approve the specific amounts. In a unanimous judgment delivered by a three-member bench, Justice Datuk Choo Kah Sing clarified a key distinction in land governance: while the National Land Council must approve the timing of a state’s revision exercise, the actual rates imposed are determined solely by the state authority under the National Land Code (NLC), FMT reported. The landowners had sought a judicial review, arguing that the hike was unlawful on four grounds: that the council had not approved the specific rates, the classification of the Genting area as “town land” was defective, the new rates were not endorsed on the land titles, and the amendments to the Pahang Land Rules were made retroactively.

items.title: House break-in in Ipoh turns fatal after suspect found dead following struggle with caretaker
items.summary: Perak Police Chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said preliminary investigations revealed that the incident is believed to have occurred at about 5 am when two suspects entered the house through a window that had been forced open, triggering a struggle with the caretaker. Members of the public with information related to the incident are urged to assist the investigation by contacting the Ipoh District Police Headquarters at 05-2451500 or visiting the nearest police station. He urged members of the public with information regarding the incident to come forward and assist the investigation by contacting the Ipoh District Police Headquarters at 05-2451500 or any nearby police station.

items.title: Inside job: MACC smashes syndicate hacking immigration system for fraudulent work passes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — A sophisticated syndicate that hacked the Malaysian Immigration System (MyIMMs) to fraudulently approve Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS) has been neutralised in a joint crackdown by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and the Immigration Department. In a statement, MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abdul Halim Aman confirmed that the detainees include two company directors, three foreigners, four Immigration officers, two officials from the department’s Information Technology Division, and a policeman. The suspects, all aged between their 30s and 40s, were apprehended between 2 p.m. and 5 p.m. at the MACC headquarters and the Immigration Department office in Penang.

items.title: Nekmat posts RM25m profit, increases dividend payout to state fishermen associations
items.summary: Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the profit had also been consistently channelled into welfare and education funds for fishermen, demonstrating Nekmat’s ability to generate returns that benefit the fishing community. Also present were Agriculture and Food Security Ministry (KPKM) secretary-general Datuk Seri Isham Ishak, Nekmat board chairman Abdul Hamid Bahari and Malaysian Fisheries Development Authority (LKIM) chairman Mohd Faiz Fadzil. Mohamad said Nekmat’s top management had last week presented proposals for projects and development programmes for fishermen’s associations nationwide involving allocations amounting to tens of millions of ringgit.

items.title: Elephant herd enters Cheneh Baharu housing area, farmers suffer RM30,000 losses
items.summary: CHUKAI, July 29 — More than 2,500 residents of Taman Gemilang Peringkat 4 in Bandar Cheneh Baharu, near here, were alarmed by the appearance of a herd of wild elephants in the housing area last Friday (July 24). Kampung Peringkat Empat, Cheneh Baharu, Federal Village Development and Security Committee (JPKKP) chairman Wan Nordin Wan Omar, 63, said the intrusion of elephants into the residential area was the second incident this year, with the first occurring in May. Fortunately, the herd left shortly after,” he said.

items.title: MetMalaysia issues widespread thunderstorm warnings across multiple states
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued thunderstorm warnings for several states, forecasting intense rainfall, strong winds, and thunderstorms across the northern, east coast, and central regions of the peninsula. The warnings, issued at 8:30am, are valid until noon today. Terengganu is similarly affected, with expected thunderstorms in Besut, Setiu, Kuala Nerus, Hulu Terengganu, Kuala Terengganu, and Marang.

items.title: Foreign couple detained over alleged abuse of two-month-old baby in Tawau
items.summary: TAWAU, July 29 — Police have detained a foreign couple in connection with the alleged abuse of a two-month-old baby girl at Batu 8, Jalan Apas, here on Monday. Acting Tawau district police chief Superintendent Wilynton Enchana Watt, in a statement, said the case came to light after a doctor at the Tawau Hospital Emergency Department lodged a police report over injuries sustained by the baby. Wilynton said that following the report, a team from the Criminal Investigation Division of the Tawau District Police Headquarters arrested the foreign man and woman, aged in his 30s and 18, respectively, at the Tawau Hospital compound at 11.45 pm.

items.title: EV charging rates remain unregulated as Malaysia leaves pricing to operators
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — The government has not introduced any price control mechanism for public electric vehicle (EV) charging services. Instead, charging rates are determined by charging station operators based on their respective commercial considerations. According to MITI, a total of 6,416 public EV chargers had been installed nationwide as of May 31, 2026.

items.title: Tok Mat warns UNHCR: Cooperate on refugee screening in Malaysia or face exit
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 29 — Malaysia should review the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees’ (UNHCR) formal presence in the country if the agency continues to resist cooperation on refugee management, said Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. The foreign minister warned that stringent screening must be a prerequisite before any UNHCR refugee cards are issued, arguing that the current lack of coordination has turned Malaysia into a “magnet” for asylum seekers, NST reported. If Malaysia had its own system, UNHCR would not need to be here,” Mimi said.

items.title: Six held, RM2.98m worth of iron ore and equipment seized in Kelantan mining raid
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, July 29 — The General Operations Force (GOF) detained six men and seized 360 tonnes of iron ore, five vehicles and an excavator worth a total of RM2.98 million during Ops Bersepadu Khazanah at a mining site in Mukim Kuala Nal, Kuala Krai, yesterday. GOF Southeast Brigade commander SAC Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the raid was carried out at 1 pm by intelligence personnel from the GOF 8th Battalion in Pengkalan Chepa in collaboration with the Kelantan Land and Mines Office (PTG). He said inspections at the site found an excavator loading iron ore onto four mototrailers.

items.title: Police arrest two express bus drivers over meth hidden in bus seat
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, July 29 — Police arrested two express bus drivers on suspicions of possessing methamphetamine found hidden in the back of the driver’s seat during an operation at the Gua Musang Rest and Relaxation Area (R&R) on Monday. Gua Musang district police chief Supt Sik Choon Foo said both men, 39 and 46, were arrested by the police after an inspection was conducted on a express bus that both of them were believed to be driving contained methamphetamine hidden the back of the driver’s seat. “Polis also seized several other items believed to be related to the investigation worth an estimated total of RM2,500,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Pahang Sultan backs community service for suitable Syariah offences
items.summary: KUANTAN, July 29 — Pahang Sultan Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri’ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah has expressed the view that community service sentences should be strengthened as an alternative approach in dealing with Syariah criminal offences. Tengku Mahkota of Pahang Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah was also in attendance. The Ruler also congratulated Pahang Royal Council, the Pahang State Secretary’s Office, the Pahang Islamic Religious Department and the Pahang Syariah Prosecution Department for being awarded the SPINE 2026 Excellent Recognition Certificate for Integrity and Governance Management Systems.

items.title: Fahmi: Negeri Sembilan election will be decided by voters, not predictions
items.summary: JEMPOL, July 29 — The outcome of an election is decided by voters, not analysts or political predictions, said Pakatan Harapan (PH) Communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said predictions by certain quarters on the outcome of the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election should be viewed as a challenge for candidates to work harder in winning the seats they are contesting. The PKR Information chief said this when commenting on predictions by Ong, the former Bangi MP, on the potential contests in several seats in the state election.

items.title: Anwar: Bangladesh seeks Petronas LNG supply to ease gas shortage
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — Bangladesh has requested assistance from Malaysia, including through collaboration with Petronas, to supply liquefied natural gas (LNG) to meet urgent needs arising from the country’s current gas supply challenges, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. In a Facebook post, Anwar said the matter was conveyed to him by Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman during a telephone conversation yesterday. “We also discussed economic cooperation, including investment developments involving Axiata and potential strategic cooperation with MMC Port to strengthen economic ties and create more opportunities for both countries,” he added.
